news.title: Messi sizzles with double in first start since World Cup final, sets Leagues Cup record
news.lede: Lionel Messi became the all-time leading scorer in the Leagues Cup after netting twice in Inter Miami's 4-2 victory over Atlético de San Luis today (Bangladesh time) in the 2026 edition's opening group matches. The Argentine superstar cancelled out the visitors' early opener in the 11th minute, finishing from Noah Allen's pass before Telasco Segovia put Miami ahead. Messi struck again just before half-time, once more converting an Allen assist, to take his Leagues Cup tally to 14 goals -- the most in the competition's history. Messi had helped Inter Miami win the 2023 Leagues Cup shortly after joining the club.

In recent decades the city of Salé, just across the river from Rabat on Morocco’s Atlantic coast, has undergone a remarkable transformation. At the start of this century it was a gritty working-class area, whose old town was still weathered enough to serve as a body double for the Somali capital Mogadishu in the film Black Hawk Down. But in recent decades, under the country’s autocratic government, the area has been transformed beyond measure, and largely beyond control.

news.title: FIFA backs Infantino, apologizes for World Cup privatization plan
news.lede: RABAT, Morocco — FIFA president Gianni Infantino has received the "full support" of senior directors on Wednesday (Thursday Manila time), but world football's governing body apologized for the controversy of the now-shelved plan to open the World Cup to private investment. Facing a barrage of criticism following the aborted plan, FIFA's leadership acknowledged "errors", while nonetheless backing under-fire Infantino following a crisis meeting in Morocco. Infantino has come under increasing pressure, even from within his organization, over his handling of the proposal, and calls for him to step down had grown since he abandoned it last Saturday. In a statement Wednesday, FIFA's leadership acknowledged "that errors were also made after the proposal was leaked to media".

news.title: FIFA apologises to members as Infantino holds crisis meeting amid stake sale fallout
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino held a crisis meeting with senior staff in Rabat, Morocco. FIFA apologised to its member associations for mistakes made over its abandoned proposal to sell commercial rights linked to the World Cup, as the governing body’s leadership reaffirmed its support for president Gianni Infantino after a crisis meeting in Morocco on Aug 5. The proposal to sell a 20 per cent stake in a new commercial rights entity to private investors in a deal that would have raised about US$4.2 billion (S$5.4 billion) provoked a fierce backlash and was withdrawn on July 31. Infantino bore the brunt of the criticism, including some from inside FIFA, which raised questions over his re-election as president next March.
